articles.title: Urnas eletrônicas passam por preparação antes das eleições em Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, 1.860 equipamentos estão sendo carregados e lacrados no polo eleitoral.
articles.summary: Ao todo, 1.860 equipamentos estão sendo carregados e lacrados no polo eleitoral.
articles.body:
Estão sendo carregados 1.860 equipamentos para as eleições deste ano — Foto: Yuri Ramos

Assistentes do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral já iniciaram os preparativos para o primeiro turno das eleições que acontecem neste domingo (4). No polo eleitoral de Campos dos Goytacazes , no Norte Fluminense, 1.860 urnas eletrônicas estão sendo carregadas.

Durante o processo, são inseridos os sistemas que serão utilizados na votação e na apuração dos votos. Depois, cada urna passa por testes automáticos para verificar se os equipamentos estão funcionando corretamente.

Após a conferência, as urnas são lacradas. Os lacres de segurança são colocados nos compartimentos dos equipamentos e impedem que eles sejam abertos ou alterados até o dia da votação.

As urnas preparadas em Campos serão distribuídas para os municípios de Campos dos Goytacazes, São Francisco de Itabapoana , Italva , Cardoso Moreira , São Fidélis e São João da Barra .

Nas eleições deste ano, os eleitores vão escolher presidente da República, governador, dois senadores, deputado federal e deputado estadual.

Com a aproximação da votação, os eleitores que ainda não definiram os candidatos têm pouco tempo para conhecer as propostas e decidir os votos.

articles.title: Polônia acusa Rússia de violar seu espaço aéreo com helicóptero | G1
articles.standfirst: Helicóptero russo violou espaço aéreo pelo exclave russo de Kaliningrado, que fica ao norte do país, segundo o Exército polonês.
articles.summary: Helicóptero russo violou espaço aéreo pelo exclave russo de Kaliningrado, que fica ao norte do país, segundo o Exército polonês.
articles.body:
Helicópteros militares Mi-8. — Foto: Vasily Fedosenko / Reuters

A Polônia acusou nesta quarta-feira (23) a Rússia de violar seu espaço aéreo com um helicóptero militar e disse que mobilizou aeronaves para responder ao incidente.

Segundo o Exército polonês, um helicóptero Mi-8 das Forças Armadas russas entrou no espaço aéreo do país pelo norte, próximo da cidade de Braniewo, e ficou durante 42 segundos antes de retornar ao exclave russo de Kaliningrado.

"O voo da aeronave foi monitorado pelos sistemas de radar das Forças Armadas da República da Polônia. Aviões de caça foram acionados, e as forças e meios terrestres permaneceram em estado de prontidão. A natureza do incidente indica que a Rússia está, mais uma vez, testando a prontidão de nossa defesa aérea", afirmou o Exército polonês em nota.

A Rússia não havia se pronunciado sobre a acusação da Polônia até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O incidente segue diversos ataques híbridos denunciados pela Europa e atribuídos à Rússia nas últimas semanas, que aumentaram as tensões entre o Kremlin e a Otan.

articles.standfirst: Segundo a Águas de Teresina, bloqueios parciais ocorrem nos bairros Mocambinho, Buenos Aires, Primavera e São Francisco, das 7h às 18h.
articles.summary: Segundo a Águas de Teresina, bloqueios parciais ocorrem nos bairros Mocambinho, Buenos Aires, Primavera e São Francisco, das 7h às 18h.
articles.body:
Obra de esgotamento sanitário executada em rua de Teresina — Foto: Divulgação/Águas de Teresina

Ruas e avenidas de quatro bairros da Zona Norte de Teresina permanecem parcialmente interditadas até este sábado (26) devido às obras de expansão da rede de esgoto. As intervenções começaram na segunda-feira (21).

Segundo a Águas de Teresina, vias dos bairros Mocambinho, Buenos Aires, Primavera e São Francisco estão com interdições parciais das 7h às 18h. Veja a lista de obras por bairro.

A concessionária informou que os trechos estão devidamente sinalizados e orientou motoristas e pedestres a redobrarem a atenção ao trafegar pelos locais, respeitando a sinalização e os bloqueios.

Além disso, recomendou que, sempre que possível, sejam utilizadas rotas alternativas. A população pode entrar em contato com a empresa pelo telefone e WhatsApp 0800 223 2000 , disponível 24 horas por dia.

*Vitória Bacelar, estagiária sob supervisão de Ilanna Serena.

articles.title: Anitta e Paolla: quem entra e quem sai das baterias no carnaval 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Paolla Oliveira volta à Sapucaí pela Imperatriz, Anitta assume o posto deixado por Virginia na Grande Rio. Confira as outras escolas que também trocaram suas rainhas para o desfile do ano que vem.
articles.summary: Rainhas de bateria Carnaval 2027: Anitta estreia na Grande Rio e Paolla Oliveira volta pela Imperatriz em meio a trocas no Grupo Especial.
articles.body:
Paolla Oliveira foi anunciada como nova rainha de bateria da Imperatriz. Atriz entra no lugar de Iza — Foto: Stephanie Rodrigues/ Rafael Nascimento/ g1

O Carnaval de 2027 terá uma nova configuração no comando das baterias das escolas de samba do Grupo Especial do Rio. Para a próxima folia, nomes conhecidos como Paolla Oliveira, Anitta, Iza, Juliana Paes e Fabíola de Andrade estão envolvidos em mudanças de postos.

A movimentação ganhou um novo capítulo nesta quarta-feira (23), com o anúncio de Paolla Oliveira como nova rainha de bateria da Imperatriz Leopoldinense. A atriz volta à Sapucaí depois de ficar fora do desfile de 2026 e assume o posto que era de Iza.

A troca é uma das principais movimentações para 2027. Iza deixou a função em março deste ano, mas continuará ligada à Imperatriz. A cantora recebeu o título de Rainha da Escola, criado especialmente para que ela permanecesse na agremiação.

Paolla, por sua vez, havia deixado a Grande Rio após o Carnaval de 2025. Antes de ser anunciada pela Imperatriz, a atriz chegou a ser cotada para retornar à escola de Duque de Caxias, mas o posto acabou ficando com Anitta.

Virginia Fonseca deixou o posto de rainha de bateria e deu lugar à Anitta na Grande Rio — Foto: Anderson Borde/AgNews/ Reprodução

Na Grande Rio, a mudança foi entre duas celebridades de perfis diferentes. Virginia Fonseca deixou o posto de rainha de bateria em agosto, após um único desfile pela escola este ano, e Anitta foi anunciada como sua substituta para o Carnaval 2027.

A cantora foi oficialmente apresentada pela agremiação em setembro e a coroação aconteceu no último domingo (20).

Imperatriz: sai Iza, entra Paolla Oliveira

Na Imperatriz Leopoldinense, Iza deixa a bateria e passa a ser Rainha da Escola. Para o posto à frente dos ritmistas, a agremiação anunciou Paolla Oliveira.

Iza havia retornado ao posto de rainha de bateria da Imperatriz em 2026. Depois do desfile, comunicou que não teria condições de manter a mesma disponibilidade por causa de novos trabalhos na música e da rotina profissional. A escola, então, criou o novo cargo para mantê-la ligada à agremiação.

A previsão é que Paolla seja coroada oficialmente em outubro, à frente da bateria Swing da Leopoldina, comandada pelo mestre Lolo.

Viradouro: sai Juliana Paes, entra Bellinha Delfim

Juliana Paes e Bellinha Delfim — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Atual campeã do Carnaval carioca, a Viradouro também terá uma nova mulher à frente da bateria em 2027.

Juliana Paes deixou o posto depois do Carnaval de 2026, quando havia retornado à função especialmente para participar do desfile que homenageou o mestre Ciça. Para 2027, a escola escolheu Bellinha Delfim como nova rainha.

Bellinha começou na Viradouro como passista, em 2019, e passou a integrar a ala de musas da escola em 2022. A escolha para o posto ocorreu depois de uma seleção organizada pela própria agremiação.

Mocidade: sai Fabíola de Andrade, entra Gaby Mendes

Gaby Mendes substituirá Fabíola Andrade na Mocidade — Foto: Reprodução e Anderson Bordê/Agnews

Na Mocidade Independente de Padre Miguel, a mudança também representa uma passagem de bastão dentro da própria escola.

Fabíola de Andrade deixou o posto de rainha de bateria e passou a ser Rainha da Escola. Para comandar a bateria Não Existe Mais Quente em 2027, a Mocidade escolheu Gabriella Mendes, conhecida como Gaby Mendes.

A nova rainha tem 23 anos e construiu sua trajetória na Mocidade como passista antes de se tornar musa. Ela foi coroada durante a semifinal do samba-enredo da escola, em agosto.

A mudança mantém uma característica que vem aparecendo em outras escolas para 2027: a valorização de nomes ligados diretamente às comunidades das agremiações.

Unidos da Tijuca: Mileide Mihaile deixa o posto

Outra mudança envolve a Unidos da Tijuca. Mileide Mihaile havia assumido o posto de rainha de bateria após a saída de Lexa, mas deixou a escola.

Rainha da Bateria Mileide Mihaile, da escola de samba Unidos da Tijuca, se apresenta durante o Carnaval do Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Pilar Olivares/Reuters

Para o Carnaval 2027, entretanto, a situação do posto mudou e a escola ainda não havia definido uma nova rainha até a publicação desta reportagem.

Até o momento, nem todas as escolas do Grupo Especial anunciaram mudanças. Entre os nomes que seguem à frente das baterias para 2027 estão:

Na Vila Isabel, Sabrina Sato se prepara para seu 15º desfile como rainha da escola. Grávida de seu segundo filho, Sato afirmou que estará à frente da Vila no próximo ano.

No Salgueiro, Viviane Araújo chegará ao 19º desfile à frente da bateria.

articles.title: Veja a entrevista de Indira Xavier no MG1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata da UP ao governo de Minas concedeu entrevista ao MG1.
articles.summary: Candidata da UP ao governo de Minas concedeu entrevista ao MG1.
articles.body:
A candidata da UP ao governo de Minas Gerais, Indira Xavier, afirmou, em entrevista ao MG1 desta quarta-feira (23), que, caso seja eleita, pretende fazer uma auditoria da dívida do estado com a União e suspender o pagamento das parcelas enquanto o processo estiver em discussão.

Ela defendeu, ainda, um maior controle estatal sobre a mineração e a participação popular em decisões do Executivo estadual.

Além das sabatinas de 30 minutos com os seis candidatos mais bem colocados na pesquisa Datafolha de 11 de setembro, exibidas ao vivo na semana passada , a Globo convidou os outros cinco concorrentes para entrevistas gravadas. As respostas somadas de cada candidato têm dois minutos.

A ordem das entrevistas foi definida por sorteio. Na segunda-feira (21), foi a vez de Ben Mendes (Missão) e, na terça (22), de Rafael Duda (PSTU) . Na quinta-feira (24), Henrique Áreas (PCO) será o entrevistado e, na sexta (25), Professor Túlio Lopes (PCB).

Veja o que Indira Xavier falou sobre os seguintes temas:

Propostas econômicas e participação popular

Questionada sobre a proposta de suspender o pagamento da dívida de Minas com a União e realizar uma auditoria nos débitos do estado, Indira Xavier afirmou que não vê risco de prejuízo às finanças estaduais.

A candidata defendeu a revisão da dívida e criticou o uso de recursos públicos para o pagamento de obrigações que considera ilegítimas. Segundo ela, Minas Gerais possui uma das maiores economias do país e deve priorizar investimentos em serviços públicos e valorização dos servidores.

"Nós não podemos ter um estado que não assegura a valorização dos servidores e a garantia dos serviços públicos, que privatiza para poder pagar uma dívida que, como foi dito, não é legítima."

A candidata disse que pretende utilizar instrumentos previstos na Constituição para realizar uma auditoria e defender a suspensão dos pagamentos enquanto o processo estiver em discussão.

"Nós usaremos o que está previsto na Constituição, que é, sim, a auditoria da dívida, a suspensão do pagamento para que a gente possa, se for para pagar de fato aquilo que é direito, que não seja sacrificando o nosso orçamento e os serviços e servidores públicos."

Ao falar sobre a proposta de suspender atividades de mineração para revisão do modelo de exploração mineral, Indira Xavier afirmou que a atividade tem sido conduzida de forma predatória em Minas Gerais e defendeu maior controle estatal sobre o setor.

A candidata citou os impactos ambientais da mineração e disse que o estado precisa garantir soberania sobre seus recursos minerais. Conforme ela, eventuais mudanças devem envolver diálogo com comunidades afetadas e municípios dependentes da atividade.

Indira também afirmou que a estatização da cadeia minerária seria uma forma de preservar empregos e garantir recursos para as cidades que dependem economicamente do setor.

"Nós precisamos diversificar a economia das nossas cidades e assegurar o controle estatal, com a participação popular, da cadeia minerária do nosso estado."

Questionada sobre a viabilidade financeira de propostas como a reestatização da Copasa, a criação de empresas públicas e a ampliação de serviços públicos, Indira Xavier afirmou que as medidas dependem de mudanças na forma de gestão do estado e de maior participação popular nas decisões.

A candidata defendeu que Minas Gerais possui riqueza suficiente para financiar investimentos públicos e criticou o modelo econômico atual, que, segundo ela, beneficia grupos que já concentram renda.

"O nosso governo propõe colocar o nosso povo no poder, e é a partir desse instrumento que nós vamos viabilizar todas as medidas econômicas que são necessárias."

Na resposta, Indira também destacou a participação feminina na política e afirmou que o combate à violência de gênero deve fazer parte das prioridades de um eventual governo.

"Eu sou a única mulher candidata nessas eleições, em uma demonstração clara de que a violência de gênero é um problema sério que nós também temos que enfrentar."

Indira Xavier, candidata ao governo de Minas pela UP — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: QUEDA DE CABELO PODE PERSISTIR MESMO QUANDO VITAMINAS ESTÃO NORMAIS; ENTENDA | G1
articles.standfirst: Exame de sangue no limite não garante que os nutrientes cheguem à raiz do cabelo; médica dermatologista explica por que o organismo prioriza órgãos vitais em períodos de sobrecarga
articles.summary: Exame de sangue no limite não garante que os nutrientes cheguem à raiz do cabelo; médica dermatologista explica por que o organismo prioriza órgãos vitais em períodos de sobrecarga
articles.body:
Saúde capilar vai muito além de checar — Foto: Divulgação

Queda de cabelo pode persistir mesmo quando vitaminas estão normais; entenda

Muitas pessoas notam uma queda intensa de cabelo e, ao fazerem o check-up, se deparam com resultados “perfeitos”. Níveis de ferro, zinco, vitamina D e hormônios da tireoide aparecem normais na folha do laboratório, mas os fios continuam caindo no banho e na escova.

A médica dermatologista Fabiana Addario (CRM 88259 | RQE 61543), especialista em Tricologia Médica e Cosmética e CEO da Clinicapelli, esclarece que essa situação é comum e tem explicação biológica direta.

“Na minha rotina clínica, ouço isso constantemente: ‘Doutora, fiz todos os exames. Tudo está perfeito no meu sangue, mas meu cabelo continua caindo. Por quê?’”, relata a médica.

Segundo a especialista, avaliar a saúde capilar vai muito além de checar se os números dos exames estão dentro da média impressa no papel.

Em situações de desgaste ou falta de energia, o organismo humano ativa um sistema de sobrevivência: ele distribui os nutrientes primeiro para as funções essenciais da vida, deixando o restante para depois.

A escala de prioridades do corpo funciona na seguinte ordem:

Órgãos vitais (coração, pulmões, cérebro e rins)

Sistema imunológico (defesa contra doenças)

Tecidos periféricos (pele, unhas e cabelo)

“O cabelo está no final da fila. Quando o corpo passa por algum estresse — físico, emocional ou infeccioso —, a primeira parte a sentir é o cabelo. Não porque falte vitamina de imediato, mas porque o organismo está concentrado em manter você vivo”, pontua a dermatologista.

Dra. Fabiana explica que o exame de sangue tradicional mostra apenas o que está circulando pelos vasos naquele instante, mas não mede se essa substância está de fato entrando nas células da raiz capilar.

“Um olhar focado em tricologia traz clareza. Não é apenas ler números, mas entender como o corpo funciona como um todo e ligar esses valores ao que vemos no couro cabeludo”, esclarece.

Um exemplo frequente envolve o ferro. Uma pessoa pode ter uma quantidade adequada do mineral no sangue, mas, se estiver com alguma inflamação no corpo, produz mais hepcidina — hormônio que controla quanto de ferro o organismo guarda e usa. Quando a hepcidina sobe, o ferro fica “preso” e não chega à raiz do cabelo, que enfraquece mesmo com o exame aparentemente normal.

Quando enfrentamos períodos prolongados de estresse — como noites mal dormidas, pressão no trabalho, pós-operatórios ou infecções recentes —, o sistema nervoso entra em alerta contínuo.

Com esse alerta, o corpo reduz o fluxo de sangue para partes menos prioritárias, como o couro cabeludo. Ao mesmo tempo, o corpo produz menos proteína nas partes que considera menos urgentes — e o cabelo é feito de proteína.

Essa resposta também eleva o cortisol — hormônio ligado ao estresse —, encurtando a fase de crescimento do fio e antecipando a fase de queda.

“É pura fisiologia. Muitas vezes não se trata de falta de vitaminas, mas de uma escolha de sobrevivência do próprio corpo”, sintetiza Dra. Fabiana.

A médica relata o atendimento recente de uma paciente de 35 anos na Clinicapelli. A mulher enfrentava queda intensa de cabelo havia quatro meses, mesmo com exames normais de ferro, zinco, vitamina D e tireoide.

Na consulta com tricoscopia — exame que amplia a imagem do couro cabeludo e dos fios em alta definição —, a Dra. Fabiana identificou inflamação leve ao redor das raízes do cabelo e fios ficando mais finos, quadro típico de eflúvio telógeno — queda temporária de cabelo, o tipo mais comum, que costuma surgir alguns meses depois de uma doença ou grande estresse.

A anamnese — entrevista detalhada sobre a rotina e o histórico da paciente — revelou que ela havia passado por uma virose três meses antes, somada a noites mal dormidas e excesso de trabalho.

Os níveis de nutrientes no sangue estavam normais para uma pessoa em repouso, mas insuficientes para um corpo em recuperação. Diante do quadro, o tratamento foi individualizado e definido após a avaliação completa, combinando orientação de cuidados em casa (o chamado home care), com ajuste personalizado de nutrientes conforme as necessidades da paciente, e protocolos de tratamento realizados dentro da clínica, que incluem tecnologias e terapia capilar. Como desfecho específico desse caso relatado pela médica, em três meses a queda cessou e o volume capilar voltou a crescer.

“Se ela tivesse apenas tomado um suplemento comum de farmácia por conta própria, não teria resolvido. O que fez diferença foi entender a causa e tratar de forma personalizada”, destaca a médica.

A especialista reforça que cada organismo responde de forma diferente e que o tratamento capilar precisa ser estritamente individualizado — não existe uma fórmula única que sirva para todos os pacientes. A conduta terapêutica só deve ser indicada por um médico após avaliação clínica presencial, uma vez que a escolha das medidas depende da causa da queda, do histórico clínico e das condições globais de saúde de cada pessoa. Por essa razão, a autoprescrição de suplementos ou medicamentos deve ser evitada.

Na Clinicapelli , a investigação dos problemas capilares reúne três passos complementares:

Tricoscopia digital : exame que amplifica o couro cabeludo e os fios, feito no próprio consultório, sem cortar nada, permitindo avaliar vermelhidão, raiz, espessura e densidade capilar.

Anamnese detalhada : conversa aprofundada para entender a linha do tempo do paciente, incluindo início da queda, infecções prévias, cirurgias, níveis de estresse e padrão de sono.

Interpretação individual dos exames : análise dos níveis no sangue de acordo com a necessidade biológica de cada organismo, sem se limitar aos padrões mínimos do laboratório.

A partir desse diagnóstico detalhado, o médico estrutura um plano terapêutico individualizado, que pode reunir orientações de cuidados diários em casa e, quando clinicamente indicado, protocolos de tratamento realizados dentro da clínica, com tecnologias e terapia capilar — sempre de acordo com a necessidade apurada em cada caso.

“Um diagnóstico de verdade não se resume a dizer que as vitaminas estão normais e que está tudo resolvido”, adverte a dermatologista.

“O cabelo é o espelho da nossa saúde geral. Quando ele cai, é sinal de que o corpo está pedindo atenção — seja por uma inflamação, alterações hormonais, estresse acumulado ou uma sobrecarga que exigiu prioridade do organismo”, conclui a Dra. Fabiana Addario.

O Ministério Público do Tocantins (MPTO) denunciou 25 pessoas investigadas na Operação Falsum Imperium por suspeita de envolvimento em um esquema de fraudes eletrônicas e lavagem de dinheiro que teria movimentado mais de R$ 10 milhões.

A denúncia foi apresentada pela 1ª Promotoria de Justiça de Araguatins. Segundo o MPTO, o grupo criava páginas e anúncios falsos que imitavam sites e serviços de empresas conhecidas para atrair consumidores interessados principalmente em passagens aéreas e rodoviárias, pacotes turísticos e outros produtos.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Os nomes dos investigados não foram divulgados e o g1 não conseguiu contato.

De acordo com a investigação, as campanhas fraudulentas chegaram a alcançar mais de três milhões de usuários nas redes sociais. Foram identificadas 1.310 transações relacionadas ao pagamento de publicidade digital, que somaram R$ 55,8 mil.

A estratégia, segundo o MPTO, era impulsionar as ofertas falsas e direcionar as vítimas para páginas de pagamento ou canais que simulavam o atendimento das empresas, inclusive pelo WhatsApp Business.

Os pagamentos eram feitos principalmente por Pix e boletos e enviados para contas utilizadas pelo grupo.

O MPTO afirma que o esquema funcionava de forma organizada e com divisão de tarefas. A denúncia aponta quatro núcleos: comando; recrutamento e gestão de contas; movimentação e triangulação financeira; e núcleo familiar e de blindagem patrimonial.

Ainda conforme a investigação, terceiros eram recrutados para fornecer documentos e dados pessoais utilizados na abertura de empresas e contas digitais. Depois de receber os valores dos golpes, o grupo teria utilizado diferentes contas, transferências e operações financeiras para dificultar o rastreamento do dinheiro.

Parte dos recursos teria sido convertida em criptoativos. Outra parcela teria sido incorporada a atividades comerciais ou utilizada na compra de veículos e imóveis.

A apuração identificou movimentações consideradas atípicas em diferentes contas. Entre elas, estão mais de R$ 4,4 milhões movimentados por uma empresa comercial, R$ 2,37 milhões em uma conta ligada a um policial penal e R$ 732 mil relacionados a um técnico em enfermagem.

Os 25 denunciados respondem, conforme a participação atribuída a cada um, por crimes relacionados à organização criminosa, estelionato qualificado por fraude eletrônica e lavagem de dinheiro.

A denúncia individualiza as condutas atribuídas aos investigados e os organiza de acordo com as funções que teriam desempenhado no esquema.

O Ministério Público também pediu à Justiça a prisão preventiva de investigados, a perda de bens relacionados aos crimes e a perda alargada de patrimônio, com o objetivo de recuperar valores apontados como provenientes das atividades ilícitas.

Em relação aos servidores públicos denunciados, o MPTO também requereu a perda dos cargos em caso de condenação. As acusações ainda serão analisadas pela Justiça. A denúncia do Ministério Público não significa condenação, e os denunciados terão direito à defesa e ao contraditório.

Mari Silva é integrante do programa de estágio entre a Rede Anhanguera e Universidade Federal do Tocantins (UFT), sob supervisão de Patricio Reis.

articles.title: Fuzis e aparelho de ultrassom são apreendidos em operação policial | G1
articles.standfirst: Material foi apreendido em Lauro de Freitas, na Região Metropolitana de Salvador. Ninguém foi preso.
articles.summary: Material foi apreendido em Lauro de Freitas, na Região Metropolitana de Salvador. Ninguém foi preso.
articles.body:
Dois fuzis, cinco sondas cirúrgicas e um aparelho de ultrassom foram apreendidos durante uma operação policial em Itinga, localidade de Lauro de Freitas , na Região Metropolitana de Salvador, na terça-feira (22). Ninguém foi preso.

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública da Bahia (SSP-BA) investiga se o kit cirúrgico apreendido seria usado para tratar suspeitos baleados em confrontos, para que eles não precisassem ser levados para hospitais.

Outra possibilidade é que o material seria revendido em Lauro de Freitas ou em cidades próximas.

Fuzis e kit cirúrgico foram apreendidos em Lauro de Freitas — Foto: SSP-BA

Todo o material foi encontrado em uma área de mata. Além dos fuzis e do kit cirúrgico, os policiais encontraram quase 200 munições, 1,8 mil porções de maconha e 2,3 mil pinos de cocaína.

Todo o material foi encaminhado à 27ª delegacia territorial, em Itinga, onde a ocorrência foi registrada.

Material cirúrgico foi encontrado pela polícia — Foto: SSP-BA

articles.title: Tech layoffs 2026: Tracking all the job losses across Xbox, Apple, Oracle, Uber, TikTok, Meta and others
articles.summary: We're more than half way through the year, and there have already been more than 185,000 layoffs across the tech industry — here's what we know.
articles.body:
We've only got a few months left in 2026, but unfortunately we didn't get here without a ton of tech layoffs. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. And not too long ago, Microsoft had its latest round of layoffs , affecting 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Shortly after, companies including Samsung, Amazon, Uber and Monday.com followed suit.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." And recently, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 185,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.title: EC 'dissent' row: Opposition seeks CEC's arrest, fresh polls in states; BJP lauds 'pure democracy' - top developments
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls triggered a major political confrontation on Wednesday, with opposition parties demanding action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically rather than under a “dictatorial” system.The political row followed a media report which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process and electoral rolls.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections indicated a breakdown in its functioning.It said differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its decisions, including those concerning SIR, had been taken unanimously.Opposition demands CEC's removal, arrestOpposition parties, which have been criticising the EC over the SIR exercise, seized on the report to renew their demands for action against Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his “vote chori” allegation against the Election Commission, describing it as “a crime against the people of India” and an attack on the Constitution.“The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” Rae Bareli MP said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said 73 Opposition Rajya Sabha MPs had submitted a fresh notice on April 24, seeking Kumar's removal.He questioned whether the Rajya Sabha chairman would decide on the pending notice since the Monsoon Session of Parliament had not yet been prorogued.Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal went further, demanding that Kumar be removed and arrested.“Gyanesh Kumar should be immediately sacked and jailed,” Thackeray said.He also demanded that the last elections in Maharashtra, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu be nullified and fresh polls held in the three states using ballot papers.Kejriwal demanded that the entire SIR exercise be cancelled, all changes made under it be reversed and the voter list from three years ago be restored. He also called for Kumar's arrest and registration of a sedition case against him.TMC MP Derek O'Brien said, “Impeach CEC to save democracy.”Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also demanded Kumar's arrest and said he had “no moral authority to continue”.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and the BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” Banerjee said.Fresh polls demanded in Bihar, West BengalThe Opposition's demands also extended to fresh elections in states where polls have already taken place.RJD leader and Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav demanded fresh elections in Bihar and West Bengal, alleging that the electoral mandates in the two states had been compromised through electoral fraud and institutional manipulation.“The opposition did not lose elections on the ground; the results were orchestrated by PM Modi and Amit Shah. In 2020, we were defeated through manipulation, and the same script was executed in 2025. Voter lists were purged, money was distributed, and counting was manipulated. The electoral outcomes in Bihar and Bengal are fraudulent, and we demand that fresh, transparent elections be held,” he said.Yadav also questioned changes to the rules governing the preservation of voting and counting records, alleging that the period had been reduced from one year to 45 days.He said this could make it difficult for parties to approach courts without access to election-related evidence.DMK president M K Stalin demanded Kumar's resignation and an immediate halt to the SIR exercise. He also sought a fair probe “into everything that transpired within the EC and those responsible should be held accountable”, according to news agency PTI.Stalin alleged that the report had raised doubts about the results of Assembly elections held after the SIR exercise and said his party had consistently opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls in the name of SIR.Akhilesh, Omar question EC functioningSamajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said governments formed during a period when the Election Commission was not functioning impartially were “unconstitutional”.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” Yadav said.He alleged that interference in the poll panel amounted to “trampling” democracy and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said the Centre and the Election Commission needed to take corrective steps to prevent people from losing faith in elections.“Corrective action needs to be taken somewhere. Otherwise, if people lose faith in elections, what remains of a democracy? Elections are the very foundations of a democracy. If people lose faith in elections, why would they even participate in them? I feel the Election Commission and the government of India need to reflect on this,” Abdullah said.He also said the report raised questions about the functioning of the poll panel and referred to his earlier concerns over the electoral process.BJP says EC differences show ‘pure democracy’The BJP rejected the Opposition's allegations and defended the reported differences between the Election Commissioners.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said differing views during official deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically.“The media reports saying that the election commissioners shared differing views in official deliberations is a reflection of pure democracy,” Patra said.“If there is no communication and exchange of views among the election commissioners who conduct polls, the opposition parties would allege 'dictatorship' and call them 'yes men' of the government,” he said.Patra said the Election Commission's response showed that neither the poll panel nor other constitutional bodies were functioning under a “dictatorial rule”.“This shows that the Election Commission (EC) and all other constitutional bodies are functioning in a democratic manner and upholding the democracy of the country,” he said.EC says all decisions were unanimousResponding to the media report, the Election Commission said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body.“The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour,” it said.The commission said all official orders, decisions and administrative directions carried full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures. It added that operational queries or inputs raised by members during the drafting stage were part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights and improving electoral processes.The EC further said differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberation before a final decision was taken.“Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorised to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system,” it said.The commission said focusing on specific internal notes and observations over 10 months while overlooking its wider body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives presented only one part of the picture.It said it had taken numerous decisions, issued instructions and introduced around 40 new initiatives and electoral reforms, including electoral-roll revision and SIR across the country.“All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,” the EC said.The commission also pointed to the conduct of elections in Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal during the period and said it remained committed to carrying out its constitutional duties.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bipartisan senators raised US journalist jailed in Iran ahead of Trump team meeting with Iranian delegation at UN
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of senators sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging action to secure the release of an American journalist unjustly imprisoned in Iran. The letter was sent one day before U.S. officials indirectly talked with Iranian officials in New York. Reza Valizadeh, 49, is a dual Iranian-American citizen and former…
articles.body:
A bipartisan group of senators sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging action to secure the release of an American journalist unjustly imprisoned in Iran. The letter was sent one day before U.S. officials indirectly talked with Iranian officials in New York.

Reza Valizadeh, 49, is a dual Iranian-American citizen and former journalist for Radio Farda, the Persian language news service housed under the U.S. Agency for Global Media. He was arrested in Iran in Sept. 2024 and is serving a 10-year prison sentence for “collaborating” with the U.S.

President Trump’s top envoys for negotiations, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, held indirect talks with Iranian officials on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday.

Asked if Valizadeh’s case was raised in the meeting, the White House pointed to Trump’s record of freeing Americans detained abroad.

“President Trump is always concerned about Americans detained abroad. That is why he has brought over 100 individuals – a record number – home from around the world,” White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly, said in a statement.

Rubio declared Valizadeh “wrongfully detained” in May 2025, making his case a priority for U.S. officials to bring up in any talks with Iranian officials.

Iran was declared a State Sponsor of Wrongful Detention on Feb. 27, the day before the U.S. and Israel launched attacks against the Islamic Republic, in a war now in its seventh month.

The designation was created by Congress and allows additional sanction authorities to isolate countries and punish their policies of unjust arrests and detentions.

“As partners in the effort to secure Mr. Valizadeh’s release, we ask that his freedom and welfare be an urgent priority through all available diplomatic channels with Iranian officials. We look forward to working with you to bring him home,” the letter read .

It was sent on Monday by Sens. Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii) and Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.). Sens. Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) and Dave McCormick (R-Penn.) also signed it. Copied on the letter were Witkoff and Adam Boehler, special envoy for hostage response; and Sebastian Gorka, deputy assistant to the president.

CBS News first reported news of the letter.

The senators raise alarm that Valizadeh is currently being held in Evin Prison, “which is notorious for its inhumane conditions and arbitrary executions of political prisoners.”

“His health has significantly deteriorated in custody, where he has consistently been denied medical care, including the inhaler he needs to treat his asthma,” they wrote.

“With every day of continued detention, Mr. Valizadeh’s life is in danger. We are extremely concerned that Iranian authorities could take sudden, arbitrary actions to endanger his life. As you know, Iran is not afraid to use American citizens as political pawns.”

articles.title: Can flurry of New York diplomacy lead to US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough?
articles.summary: Analysts say a deal this week is unlikely – core disagreements between Washington and Tehran remain unresolved.
articles.body:
At the colloquium established shortly after the second world war to prevent future wars, United States President Donald Trump did just the inverse: He platformed his unceasing threats against Iran, suggesting almost casually on Tuesday that he could “ annihilate ” the country he has waged war against since February 28.

But behind closed doors on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) , a flurry of diplomatic activity concerning the ongoing US-Iran war has also been unfolding, as world leaders gather in New York.

The US and Iran held indirect talks for three hours on Tuesday. US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with Trump calling it a “ very good ” and “very productive” meeting. Trump also met Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) leaders that day, with senior officials from the region mulling a Qatari proposal for a common security framework involving Iran and the Gulf states.

Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arrived in New York early on Wednesday – the first time a leader whose country is at war with the US has set foot on US soil to address the gathering. And Chinese President Xi Jinping will skirt New York to instead meet Trump one-on-one in Washington, DC – his first state visit to the US in just less than a decade. Xi lands on Wednesday evening.

All these separate diplomatic initiatives, analysts tell Al Jazeera, are parts of a push to bring Iran and the US back to the negotiating table. According to Al Jazeera’s correspondent in Tehran, Tohid Asadi, Araghchi’s meeting with Witkoff and Kushner was to convey Tehran’s latest set of conditions to end the war , following the collapse of the June 60-day memorandum of understanding (MoU) finalised in Islamabad, Pakistan.

But analysts say expecting an actual deal to emerge this week from the diplomatic meetings in the US would be unrealistic. Multiple actors and mediators in the conflict are testing possible off-ramps, but core disagreements between Washington and Tehran remain unresolved.

“I am sceptical that a breakthrough deal can emerge this week, but a series of understandings can build confidence for renewed diplomacy,” Sanam Vakil, the director of the Middle East and North Africa Programme at Chatham House, told Al Jazeera.

Vakil is hesitant to call the current moment ripe for a diplomatic breakthrough – it is far too early, and there is a history of negotiations failing, she said.

“Both sides have been negotiating for over two years and on two occasions, that ended with military conflict and these negotiations continue amid persistent military threats,” she said.

Iran has long pointed to its previous rounds of diplomatic talks with the US – in 2025 and again this year – as evidence that Washington can veer from negotiations to military action. It has cited the 12-day war last June, and the current conflict, which began with joint US-Israeli strikes on Tehran at a time Washington and Tehran were engaged in Oman-mediated dialogue.

Adel Abdel Ghafar, a senior fellow focusing on the Middle East at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute, said that there appears to be “genuine” movement towards reigniting negotiations – but also “a fair amount of posturing”. He referenced Trump’s praise for Tuesday’s indirect Iran-US talks and his pugnacious UNGA speech the same day.

A breakthrough hinges on whether Iran’s diplomats in New York can actually deliver, he said.

“Araghchi and Pezeshkian can negotiate, but any deal will need the consent of the [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] and the hardliners in charge of the war back home,” Abdel Ghafar told Al Jazeera.

There are specific indicators to watch for another round of US-Iran contact, the analysts said.

“The signs to watch for are another confirmed round of US-Iran talks, agreement on sequencing or reciprocal steps, and language from both sides becoming more specific about implementation rather than simply repeating maximalist demands,” said Vakil.

Abdel Ghafar added that, against the backdrop of UNGA, signs could include Araghchi or Pezeshkian meeting directly with US officials, in addition to supportive statements from more hardline elements of the Iranian administration back home.

The appearance of such indicators could lead to a stronger push for such talks when Trump meets Xi, as well as an easing of fighting between the Iran-backed Houthi group and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, which has escalated in recent weeks , the analyst added.

The limits of Gulf and Chinese diplomacy

The analysts agreed that the Gulf states remain crucial in brokering a return to talks because they have channels to both warring sides, as well as a very strong interest in preventing further escalation, having absorbed the cost of the fighting since February. Qatar , Oman and other Gulf states have been involved in mediation efforts throughout the conflict.

“Qatar and Oman, in particular, can help translate broad political messages into workable arrangements on issues such as Hormuz and regional security,” said Vakil.

China, meanwhile, has less capacity or interest to mediate, she argued.

Beijing, however, could use its economic and political leverage with Tehran “to encourage compromise and give Iran greater confidence that any agreement will not leave it completely isolated”, said Vakil.

Abdel Ghafar pointed out that China remains Iran’s main customer for its oil, explaining why Beijing has pushed for a return to the June interim deal and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

“Still, I think neither can impose a settlement – it ultimately comes down to Washington and Tehran,” he said.

The tit-for-tat rhetoric has resulted in continued deadlock in the conflict, with each side unwilling to relinquish to the other’s demands and appear to admit defeat.

On Tuesday, following Trump’s remarks on annihilating Iran, Iran’s military warned that it is ready to respond with “crushing” attacks more severe than earlier in the war.

“The main challenge is finding a formula that both governments can present domestically as a negotiated compromise rather than capitulation,” said Vakil.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a key obstacle.

“It’s Iran’s strongest card and the thing Washington most wants back, with oil prices high and midterms approaching,” said Abdel Ghafar.

“Tehran will be reluctant to give it up without firm guarantees in return.”

Still, he warned that even if Washington and Tehran de-escalate, that does not automatically extend to the Red Sea.

The wider landscape of regional instability and conflict has created new conditions for Yemen’s unresolved war to flare up once again. The Bab al-Mandeb, now under effective Houthi control, has gained greater significance amid Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital artery for global oil and gas supplies.

“Calm in Hormuz won’t necessarily mean calm in Bab al-Mandab,” said Abdel Ghafar.

articles.title: Fire hydrants lacking water flow needed for firefighting - NFCC
articles.summary: Inadequate water supplies are "affecting fire crews' ability" to respond to incidents, say fire chiefs.
articles.body:
Fire hydrants in the UK often do not provide enough water flow for firefighting, fire chiefs have warned.

A report published by the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) claims that inadequate water supplies across the UK are impacting fire crews' "ability to respond effectively" and putting the public at risk.

It carried out a survey of UK fire services which suggested that 81% have had to change their emergency response plans due to concerns over adequate water supplies.

"The very least firefighters should be able to rely on is access to the water they need to protect people," said NFCC chairman Phil Garrigan.

The report calls for firefighting water supplies to be recognised as a critical public safety requirement, for "greater accountability" for the water sector and for increased hydrant maintenance.

Fire hydrants in the UK are access points that allow crews to access mains water when they arrive at the scene of a blaze. They are often marked by a yellow sign showing a capital "H" - there are hundreds of thousands across the UK.

The NFCC warned that climate change, droughts and population growth are "increasing demand on an already stretched water network".

It provided the example of West Midlands Fire Service, which experienced water pressure issues over several days during the major wildfire in Stourbridge last month.

During the height of the blaze, it took 40 minutes to refill its water carrier due to reduced pressure - and crews had to rely on an additional high-volume pump for water supply.

"Firefighters cannot fight fires without water," said Mr Garrigan.

"That sounds obvious, yet our evidence shows four in five fire and rescue services have had to change response plans because of concerns about firefighting water supplies," he said.

"The demands on fire and rescue services are growing, with larger wildfires, extreme weather and increasingly complex risks."

"As the task becomes more challenging, the very least firefighters should be able to rely on is access to the water they need to protect people and property."

The NFCC's survey, conducted over summer and which received responses from 50% of UK fire services, found that half of fire services it heard from "frequently encounter insufficient flow".

It also suggested that a third of water companies cannot increase water flow when needed.

The NFCC said these factors have led to "workarounds", increased demand on resources and "reduced resilience" when responding to incidents.

The organisation has called on water regulators to enforce measures on water providers regarding the provision of water for firefighting, and to implement "clear national standards" on fire hydrant repair and maintenance.

It also urged the UK government to ensure that fire and rescue services are recognised as "key stakeholders" within the water sector.

In response, Ofwat said it would consider the points raised in the NFCC's report and added that water companies do "have a duty to supply fire and rescue services to support firefighting".

"We would expect water companies and fire services to work together to ensure this is the case," a spokesperson said.

articles.title: How much is UK supporting Saudi Arabia in its war with Iran-backed Houthis?
articles.summary: UK to refuel Saudi fighter jets and France to secure energy infrastructure amid fighting with Yemen’s Houthi group.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom will provide Saudi Arabia with military support in its escalating war against Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi group, the British government said this week.

The UK agreed to provide air-to-air refuelling of Saudi fighter jets that are conducting missions after the kingdom requested air-defence support, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday.

However, it will not directly join Riyadh’s renewed conflict with the Houthis, which began in 2014 after the Houthis seized Yemen’s capital Sanaa along with large areas of northwest Yemen, driving the internationally recognised government to Aden. The two sides had reached a United Nations-mediated ceasefire in 2022, before fighting broke out again this year amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

Particularly heavy fighting erupted again two weeks ago as the Houthis advanced against Yemeni forces to the Red Sea coast, taking the strategic port city of Mocha and Mayyun Island in the middle of the Bab al-Mandeb, the entry point for shipping entering the Red Sea from the south.

Since then, the group has targeted Riyadh as well as Saudi oil infrastructure, including taking out a section of the vital East-West Pipeline that had allowed Saudi to make oil exports despite disruption in the Strait of Hormuz triggered by the Iran war.

Before the latest bout of fighting broke out, the Houthis had also declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Red Sea, through which about 12 percent of global trade passes.

Here is what you need to know about what support the UK will provide:

British PM Burnham said London had accepted a Saudi request for what he called “defensive air-to-air refuelling”. Britain will deploy one Royal Air Force Voyager tanker aircraft to assist with this in the coming days.

“We have received a request from the kingdom of Saudi Arabia for military support,” Burnham told reporters on his way to the UN General Assembly in New York this week, adding that he had agreed to the request on the advice of his defence and foreign secretaries.

Burnham said the arrangement would be “time-limited” and would be kept under review. However, the UK’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) has not specified a timetable.

Burnham said the UK was “acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region”, linking the need to keep oil export routes open.

In a statement, the MoD told Al Jazeera that the decision to provide support “builds on the UK’s existing military contribution to Saudi Arabia’s air defence”, including the deployment of “air defence equipment and UK personnel helping to protect against missile and drone attacks”.

“Saudi Arabia and Yemen are long-standing partners of the United Kingdom, and play a vital role in regional stability. It is in the UK’s interest to protect regional stability, protecting vital trade and energy supplies and encouraging a diplomatic resolution to the conflict in Yemen,” the MoD said.

Air-to-air refuelling is the transfer of aviation fuel from one aircraft to another in mid-air.

Refuelling in mid-air will allow Saudi fighter jets to remain airborne past their fuel limits, in order to spend more time patrolling Saudi airspace or responding to incoming threats.

Saudi Arabia faces potential threats to cities, military installations and energy infrastructure spread across a very large area.

While the Houthis have largely targeted Saudi cities in the south of the country, close to the Yemeni border, they have hit targets in the capital city, Riyadh, in the country’s centre.

During Israel’s war on Gaza, the Houthis also launched missiles towards Israel.

What’s the UK-Saudi Arabia military relationship?

Britain has particularly deep military ties with Saudi Arabia, one of the biggest buyers of British military equipment, stretching back for decades.

Under the Conservative Party government of John Major in the 1990s, and the later Labour governments of Tony Blair and Gordon Brown from the late 1990s to 2010, the UK supplied Tornado and Hawk aircraft and other equipment to the kingdom, involving the UK defence company BAE Systems.

The relationship was expanded to include Eurofighter Typhoon combat aircraft. In 2006, Saudi Arabia agreed to buy 72 Typhoons in a deal worth $40bn that also included technology transfer and training.

London has also provided defensive assistance during the ongoing regional conflict. Earlier this year, the UK deployed its Sky Sabre air-defence system to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom from Iranian missile attacks on United States military assets and other infrastructure on Saudi territory.

The air refuelling assistance from London could improve Saudi Arabia’s ability to defend itself to some degree, but what the UK has announced so far is limited, experts say.

The UK’s support carries more political weight than military significance, according to Chris Doyle, director of the Council for Arab-British Understanding.

“In military terms this is not a major change-up,” Doyle said, arguing that what matters more for Saudi Arabia right now is having visible international backing as it confronts the Houthis.

Riyadh will be keen to avoid appearing “isolated” in the conflict, particularly as other countries remain reluctant to become directly involved, he said. Most significantly, the administration of US President Donald Trump has already indicated it will not involve itself in the Saudi-Houthi fighting or against Houthi blockades on Saudi-linked shipping in the Red Sea.

Trump said the Houthis had assured US officials that they had no intention of attacking US shipping in the Red Sea.

As for other states, “Many are reluctant to get involved. They see this as being part of the wider US-Iran conflict, and they just are hesitant,” Doyle said.
